| Keyword | Pkg | Δ | Change | Migration | Ref |

| `PLATFORM_HRP_MAINNET` / `PLATFORM_HRP_TESTNET` | dpp | ± | bech32m HRP constants changed: mainnet `"evo"` → `"dash"`, testnet/devnet/regtest `"tevo"` → `"tdash"`. ⚠ PR #3059 says "Breaking Changes: None, but this unbreaks a breaking change", but every v3.0.0-encoded address string changes; a reviewer flagged the missing backward compat and the author deferred it to a later PR | re-encode stored/displayed addresses with `PlatformAddress::to_bech32m_string`; update any hard-coded `evo1…`/`tevo1…` strings and prefix checks to `dash1…`/`tdash1…` | [PR:3059] [C:961fe9e] |
| `PlatformAddress::from_bech32m_string` | dpp | ± | only accepts the `dash`/`tdash` HRPs, so `evo1…`/`tevo1…` strings now fail with `ProtocolError::DecodingError` ("invalid HRP"); payload type byte parsed inline as `P2PKH_TYPE` (0xb0) / `P2SH_TYPE` (0x80). `to_bech32m_string` emits `dash1…`/`tdash1…` with different checksums | no fallback for old HRPs: convert legacy strings yourself (decode the bech32m payload, re-encode with the new HRP) | [PR:3059] [C:961fe9e] |
| `PlatformAddress::to_bytes` | dpp | ± | storage/raw byte format changed: the first byte is now the bincode variant index (`0x00` P2PKH, `0x01` P2SH) instead of `P2PKH_TYPE`/`P2SH_TYPE` (`0xb0`/`0x80`). `PlatformAddress::from_bytes` now decodes via bincode and rejects `0xb0`/`0x80`-prefixed bytes. `base64_string_with_nonce` output changes with it | re-serialize any persisted v3.0.0 `to_bytes()` output; `P2PKH_TYPE`/`P2SH_TYPE` now apply only to bech32m strings, not raw bytes | [PR:3059] [C:961fe9e] |
| `MAX_P2SH_SIGNATURES` | dpp | + | new `pub const MAX_P2SH_SIGNATURES: usize = 17` (16 keys + CHECKMULTISIG dummy) in `address_funds::witness` | none (additive) | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `AddressWitness::P2sh` | dpp | ± | bincode `Decode`/`BorrowDecode` and serde `Deserialize` now reject a `signatures` vector longer than `MAX_P2SH_SIGNATURES`. Encoding is still unbounded | cap P2SH witnesses at 17 signatures before serializing, or the receiver cannot decode them | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `WithdrawalBelowMinAmountError` | dpp | + | new basic consensus error (code 10818) with `new(withdrawal_amount, min_amount, max_amount)` and getters `withdrawal_amount()`, `min_amount()`, `max_amount()`. Despite its name, it is also raised when the amount is above the maximum | handle code 10818 in client error mapping | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `BasicError::WithdrawalBelowMinAmountError` | dpp | + | new variant on `BasicError`, which is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so exhaustive `match`es stop compiling | add a match arm (wasm-dpp needed the same fix) | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `AddressCreditWithdrawalTransitionV0` | dpp | ± | `validate_structure` now rejects `input_sum <= output_amount` with `WithdrawalBalanceMismatchError` and withdrawal amounts outside `MIN_WITHDRAWAL_AMOUNT`..`system_limits.max_withdrawal_amount` with `WithdrawalBelowMinAmountError`. `core_fee_per_byte = 0` is now rejected (non-zero Fibonacci check) | make sure inputs exceed the change output by a withdrawal amount within the limits; use a non-zero Fibonacci `core_fee_per_byte` | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `is_fibonacci_number` | dpp | − | module `dpp::util::is_fibonacci_number` removed (renamed) | use `dpp::util::is_non_zero_fibonacci_number::is_non_zero_fibonacci_number`, which returns `false` for 0 | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `is_non_zero_fibonacci_number` | dpp | + | replaces `is_fibonacci_number`: returns `false` for 0 and uses integer Newton square root (the f64 `sqrt` gave false positives above 2^52) | none beyond the rename above | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `StateTransitionWitnessValidation::validate_witnesses` | dpp | ± | now returns `InvalidStateTransitionSignatureError` when the witness count ≠ input count (before, `zip` silently validated only the shorter list, so 0 witnesses passed) | provide exactly one witness per input | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `deduct_fee_from_outputs_or_remaining_balance_of_inputs` | dpp | ± | behavior fix: fee-strategy indices now resolve against a snapshot of input/output keys taken before mutation. Before, draining an entry shifted later indices, so fees hit the wrong address (consensus-visible) | none for callers. Fee results differ from v3.0.0 when a fee step drains an entry | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |

| `AddressFundingFromAssetLockTransitionAction::input_contributions_total` | drive | + | new accessor returning the total credits contributed from address inputs | none (additive) | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |

| `AddressFundingFromAssetLockTransitionAction::resolved_outputs` | drive | ± | the remainder output is now computed from asset lock value + `input_contributions_total` (before, it used only the asset lock value, which broke credit conservation when address inputs were present) | none. Remainder amounts differ from v3.0.0 when address inputs are present | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `Drive::set_balance_to_address` | drive | ± | this and `set_balance_to_address_operations` now return `ProtocolError::Overflow` when the balance is above `i64::MAX` (sum-tree limit) instead of casting unchecked | handle the new error. Upstream validation should already prevent such balances | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
| `AddressCreditWithdrawalTransitionActionV0::try_from_transition` | drive | ± | this and `IdentityCreateFromAddressesTransitionActionV0::try_from_transition` / `IdentityTopUpFromAddressesTransitionActionV0::try_from_transition` now use checked arithmetic and return an `OverflowError` consensus error on input-sum overflow or output > inputs (before: unchecked `sum()` / subtraction) | none. Expect `OverflowError` in the validation result instead of a panic or wrapped value | [PR:3053] [C:d12124e] |
